::: {#def-bootstrap-distribution}
#### Bootstrap distribution

Let $\hparam$ be a statistic computed from the observed data.
Draw $B$ independent [bootstrap samples](#def-bootstrap-sample),
and compute the statistic on each one,
giving $\hparam^*_1, \ldots, \hparam^*_B$.
The **bootstrap distribution** of $\hparam$
is the [empirical distribution](nonparametric-models.qmd#def-empirical-distribution) of $\hparam^*_1, \ldots, \hparam^*_B$.

Source: @wikipedia_bootstrapping_statistics.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {#rem-bootstrap-distribution-role}
#### What the bootstrap distribution estimates

The bootstrap distribution estimates the [sampling distribution](estimation.qmd#def-sampling-distribution)
of $\hparam$.
The observed sample stands in for the population,
and resampling from it stands in for drawing new samples
from the population.
:::
